about: Native-only text substitutions for the pinned YR tree (yr/ra2-decomp, yr/tibsun headers; lane Y1), applied by native/yr/tools/yr_units.py before the port rewrites, where clang rejects VC6 dialect. 'file' is a path under the tree's header directory ('hdr/<name>') or its sources ('src/<path>'), or '*' for every file; 'old' is literal text (every occurrence; a fixup that matches nothing fails the generation), or with 'regex': true a Python regular expression. Each keeps the original behaviour; 'why' says how. Like native/port/fixups.json for the RA2 tree, it never edits yr/. A row with 'cut' instead of 'old' removes the function whose marker (// FUNCTION: GAMEMD <address>) it names, up to the next marker or the end of the file; native/yr/glue supplies the native version. A row with 'skip_unit' leaves that source out of the native build (its functions are link-closure traps until native/yr/glue or a later stage supplies them).

fixups.old: friend Int<PRECISION> Generate_Prime(Straw & rng, int pbits, Int<PRECISION> const * = 0);
fixups.new: friend Int<PRECISION> Generate_Prime(Straw & rng, int pbits, Int<PRECISION> const *);

Get_RDTSC_CPU_Speed measures the x86 time-stamp counter (inline assembly); natively the counter is a virtual 1 GHz clock and the glue returns its rate, 1000, as the RA2 native tree does.

A TStringID object passed through a debug print's varargs: VC6 copied its bytes onto the stack, so %s read its first four bytes as a pointer; clang refuses a class through varargs (and would trap). The name's text is what the message wants; the print is the debug output (FUN_004068E0).

A Wstring object passed to %s: VC6 pushed the object's bytes and the format read the first four as its value, which is the Wstring's text pointer (its first member). clang refuses a class through varargs; get() passes that pointer.
A timer object passed to %d: VC6 pushed the object's bytes and the format read the first four as its value (the timer's first field); the cast reads the same four bytes.

Darwin's headers define BIG_ENDIAN (4321) on every machine (machine/endian.h, with LITTLE_ENDIAN and BYTE_ORDER); the packet union's byte order is chosen by the machine's actual order, little-endian on arm64 as on x86. Without this the base64 decoder swapped bytes and the encryption keys (Init_Keys) decoded to nothing.
